main_body: Shrine hall: a large green tiled hip roof (rows 4-42) over a red beam, white plaster walls with red posts, a dark lattice door and a stone base
top_band: Green tile roof slope with a lighter ridge cap, rows 4-42 in the centre column; tiles run from light to dark green, ending in light eave tiles at row 41
evidence: In the middle column the lit ridge cap (rows 4-8) leads into a long tiled slope (rows 8-42). A red beam at rows 43-46 marks the front edge. Below it is the south wall (rows 47-73) with posts, an inset dark lattice door and a stone base. The roof reads as a real sloping surface seen from above, like the reference houses. A separate dark eave shadow is weak, but the red beam gives a clear step and the doors sit inset between the posts.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps with per-tile highlights and dark gaps, matching the scalloped tile texture of the references. The plaster wall has speckle and the stone base has varied blocks. The door lattice, wood posts and gold rope add detail. The outline mixes dark brown and dark green-purple tones with some very dark edges at the roof sides. It is not a uniform black sticker outline. Overall it is as rich as the references.
